text:
Seattle had the better of the first period and still trailed by the time Berkly Catton scored. Kirill Kaprizov put MIN ahead 26 seconds in, and Catton, the Kraken's No. 8 pick in 2024 who arrived from a 109-point season with Spokane of the WHL, tied it at 10:13 of the first on a chance that rated at just 5%. That was the last good news SEA got. MIN scored four more times and won 5-1.

The second period decided it. After a first period in which SEA led the chance count 1.16 to 0.78 in expected goals (a measure of shot quality), MIN flipped it to 2.68 to 0.38. Blake Coleman made it 2-1 early in the period, Olli Maatta scored on a 2% look at 11:33, and Joel Eriksson Ek made it 4-1 at 13:00. Coleman added an empty look at the end, a 91% chance in the third, for his second of the night. Over the full game MIN took 74 shot attempts to 50, and our numbers say MIN deserved to win 84% of the time, meaning it won that share of simulated replays of every shot.

The goaltending sharpened the gap. Jesper Wallstedt stopped 23 of 24 and saved about one goal more than the shots he faced should have allowed. Joey Daccord stopped 31 of 35 and was close to par, so the damage was mostly in front of him. Kaprizov and Eriksson Ek each had a goal and an assist, with Kaprizov's line owning roughly 3.06 expected goals to 0.23 against while he was on the ice. We have no streaks or records in our facts to place this result in the standings, but MIN leaves Seattle with the kind of two-way dominance that travels, while SEA has a quiet 24 shots to explain.
